rule_level_problems.problem: The page's 'or exposure to possible allergen' (footnote 3: medications, new food or insect bite/sting within the last few hours) has no counterpart. Only the insect bite/sting case is implicitly covered by the trigger; a bite/sting patient who also took a new medication or food is not caught. Page 20 shows the representable form (finding Exposure to ... Drug or medicament).

Footnote 2 says 'shock likely' from SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness. No probable Shock rule exists, so the Urgent rule's Shock arm fires only when a clinician records Shock directly; of the five footnote criteria only SBP < 80 is in the Urgent rule, and confusion is not checked for at all.

A single sudden-onset symptom (cough, nausea, diarrhoea, chest pain) after any bite/sting yields probable Anaphylaxis and hence Urgent. This is the page's literal 'any of' wording, so it is not an encoding error, but it is far looser than the gold page-20 rule (two symptom groups) and will over-diagnose anaphylaxis rather than merely flag urgency. A reconciler may prefer to put the 18 symptoms directly in the Urgent rule's 'or' and leave the anaphylaxis diagnosis to page 28.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable cellulitis after bite/sting; Diagnose probable anaphylaxis after bite/sting
rule_level_problems.problem: Both probable rules use Bite - wound / Venomous sting as evidence, but those findings appear only in the task's due_to, not in its check_for (they cannot be in both: a task may not check for its own due_to). Whether the 'probable evidence must be checked for in the same file' test accepts the task trigger as coverage is not verifiable from the inputs I may open; flagged so the gate run confirms it.

'Weakness' is encoded as Muscle weakness only. SNOMED also has 'Weakness present' and 'Asthenia' (findings) that are not descendants of Muscle weakness, so a record using either will not satisfy the Urgent rule.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully: every one of the 13 criteria elements is in check_for and in the Urgent rule with existing, well-chosen SNOMED concepts, and the two 'likely' diagnoses outside the box (papular urticaria, cellulitis) are correct probable rules. The most consequential gap is the dropped 'exposure to possible allergen' arm of the anaphylaxis criterion, followed by the footnote-2 'shock likely' definition, which has no probable Shock rule and leaves confusion, pulse and respiratory rate unused. Lower-severity notes: the single-symptom anaphylaxis rule is very loose (though literal to the page), and 'Weakness' only matches Muscle weakness.
